# Playnite Library Server

Playnite extension that serves your game library over local HTTP.

[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Garulf/playnite-library-server)](https://github.com/Garulf/playnite-library-server/blob/main/LICENSE)

[![Buy Me a Coffee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Buy%20Me%20a%20Coffee-support-FFDD00?logo=buy-me-a-coffee)](https://www.buymeacoffee.com/garulf) [![Sponsor](https://img.shields.io/github/sponsors/Garulf?logo=githubsponsors)](https://github.com/sponsors/Garulf)

## What it does

Runs a loopback-only HTTP server inside Playnite so other local tools, such as the
[Flow Launcher Playnite plugin](https://github.com/Garulf/Playnite-Plugin), can read the
live game library without opening the LiteDB-locked `games.db`. It listens on
`http://localhost:38217/` (port configurable in the extension settings, restart Playnite after
changing it), binds only to localhost, and serves a single read-only endpoint. Nothing about
launching or installing games goes through it.

## Endpoint

`GET /games` returns the library as a JSON array. Hidden games are excluded unless you ask for
them with `GET /games?hidden=true`. Any other path returns a 404 with a JSON error body.

Each game object has these fields:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | Playnite game id (GUID) |
| `name` | string | |
| `isInstalled` | bool | |
| `hidden` | bool | |
| `installDirectory` | string or null | |
| `icon` | string or null | relative media path under Playnite's `library\files` |
| `coverImage` | string or null | same convention as `icon` |
| `playtime` | number | seconds |
| `lastActivity` | string or null | UTC ISO 8601 |
| `links` | array | `{name, url}` objects |
| `source` | string or null | source library name, e.g. `Steam` |

## Installation

Download `PlayniteLibraryServer_<version>.pext` and open it with Playnite (or drag it onto the
Playnite window), then restart Playnite.

## Building

```
./build.sh   # builds Release and packs PlayniteLibraryServer_<version>.pext
./test.sh    # runs the NUnit suite
```

Requires the .NET SDK. On Linux, running the net462 tests additionally needs `mono` and an SDK
that ships the .NET Framework test host; `test.sh` picks up an SDK in `~/.dotnet` automatically
if present.
